requirements.statement: A game build is a folder of static files; upload accepts a folder or zip, and an uploaded build can contain up to 1 GB uncompressed.
The default entry point is `index.html`; `wavedash.toml` may set `entrypoint` to an HTML (`.html`/`.htm`) or JavaScript (`.js`) file relative to `upload_dir`.
The host injects the `Wavedash` SDK global; every game must call `Wavedash.init()` once when ready to show, while installing `@wvdsh/sdk-js` is optional.
The uploaded-build limit is 1 GB uncompressed; the public upload documentation gives no per-file or file-count limit.

Developer Portal upload accepts a build folder or zip; CLI flow uses `wavedash build push` then `wavedash publish <BUILD_ID>`, and local SDK testing uses `wavedash dev`; verify the published game at its public game URL.
CLI configuration supports `game_id`, `upload_dir`, and optional `entrypoint` in root `wavedash.toml`; `upload_dir` is relative to the config file.
requirements.detail: wavedash.toml: upload_dir ./upload, no game_id (the push run sets it)

requirements.statement: Wavedash runs games cross-origin isolated and requires external servers contacted by the game to send `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin` and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on every response; the docs do not specify a `connect-src` CSP policy or enumerate allowed WebSocket/WebRTC destinations.

Published Wavedash games can be embedded in an iframe; the documented embed code uses `https://wavedash.com/embed/games/<slug>` and an `allow` attribute including `autoplay`, `fullscreen`, `gamepad`, `cross-origin-isolated`, `pointer-lock`, and other listed permissions; the embedding page is instructed to keep that attribute.
Wavedash serves the game origin from a subdomain of `builds.wavedashcdn.com`.
The published-game embed example does not document the Wavedash frame's `sandbox` attribute, the frame's response CSP, or a `Permissions-Policy` response header.
